newsitem.title: USA: Florida sees N.C. ruling benefiting its case.
newsitem.headline: Florida sees N.C. ruling benefiting its case.

text.p: Karen Pankowski, spokeswoman for Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles, said the governor was elated by the news a North Carolina judge had ruled the Food and Drug Administration has authority to regulate cigarettes.
"This confirms what the governor has been saying, that tobacco is a drug and is addictive," she said.
She also expected the ruling to help Florida's efforts to sue tobacco companies to recoup the public health costs of tobacco-related illnesses.
"This bolsters our lawsuit and exposes the deception and hypocrisy of cigarette manufacturers," she said.

Florida is suing the tobacco industry for some $1.4 billion it says it has spent to treat tobacco-related illnesses since 1994. The civil lawsuit filed in a West Palm Beach circuit is set to go to trial in August.
The state also has said its attorney general, Robert Butterworth, is involved in negotiations for a tobacco industry settlement of litigation against it.
